items.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
items.q: Mr. White, in a milk dairy, hired me to work for him.

ctx.x: That's the one you got now? No, that's not the one I got now. This was a assignment that I had. It sounded like an electric box. She sold it to me and she said, I paid, well, in that time, you could get a guitar, a cheap can, for about $50 or $60. She told me she'd pay $60 for that guitar. She said, that son of mine is not interested in you. She said, I said, for $4. She sold it to me. For $4? $4. So I'd taken that guitar and I went on, went on. I got more and more with it, you know? items.title: Angola Talking Interview, 1959-03-15
items.q: Mr. White, he knows me. He hollered, Pete, and I said, yes, sir.

ctx.x: Be here three years. Three years, six the next month. And this is your first time in annual? First time, I was in trouble. First time you ever been in trouble and you got lied. Yes, got lied. Oh, yes.

Well, I got this live here. I walked in the store, had a beer garden on the side of the store, you know? And two fellows leaning up on the bar and one of them asked me why that I came from. And I told him I came from Zachary. Well, he cussed me a time or two and told me I didn't come to Zachary. I told him, yes, I did. So he cussed me again. I said, well, I wouldn't call you that. So he said, let me tell you one thing. He said, you better go back to Zachary and pick some more cut, because you want to do slicker.…
